surface_decisions.reason: The human front door must expose the new L6 candidate while clearly separating Draft candidate from current capability.
The existing workflow already builds the repository README for Draft inspection and restricts production deployment to main; no workflow contract or render source changed.
If accepted and merged, the README-derived production homepage must expose the candidate-as-current transition; Draft work cannot attest that future deployment.
Current-state authority must record that 121Q28 is open and not part of the current capability baseline.
Human navigation needs candidate method, example and template links without promoting them to current architecture.
The L6 usage interface now needs an executable candidate path and explicit horizontal-versus-vertical and non-proof boundaries.
Human AI users need the backstage interface and warnings against fixed outlines, stock imagery and literary-quality automation.
Cold-start AI must locate the candidate and preserve its Draft, L6-only and non-proof status.
Agent handoff must preserve the method gates, Q27 freeze and no-current-capability boundary.
Machine readers need a compact path and explicit constraints for the new candidate interface.
Unreleased history must record the candidate addition and its non-current boundary.
Versioning must state that 0.1.0 is a candidate L6 interface rather than an architecture-version upgrade.
